name: Nauders
kurzbeschreibung: The sunniest spot in Tirol, with over 300 sunny days, right on the border with Italy and Switzerland.
text:
Overview

Nauders is situated in the Tyrolean Oberland on a sun-drenched plateau at an altitude of 1,394 meters, immediately north of the Reschen Pass at the historic border triangle between Austria, Italy, and Switzerland. Located in the Landeck district, this vibrant community is home to roughly 1,560 residents and spans over 90 square kilometers. As a time-honored Alpine pass village, Nauders blends rich transit heritage with world-class holiday infrastructure, renowned as a snow-sure year-round outdoor hub. The dramatic mountain landscape surrounding the village stretches from the Ötztal Alps to the Sesvenna range, offering magnificent panoramas. With its distinctive blend of Rhaeto-Romanic architecture, Alpine farming heritage, and proximity to South Tyrol's Vinschgau and the Swiss Engadine, Nauders radiates a uniquely cosmopolitan mountain flair.

History

The settlement history of Nauders began in antiquity, with the historic Roman imperial highway Via Claudia Augusta traversing the Reschen Pass directly through the municipal lands around 50 AD. The first written documentation dates to 1150 under the name 'Nudres', an ancient Rhaetian toponym. For centuries, Nauders functioned as a key strategic checkpoint for trans-Alpine commerce. Rising above the southern edge of town, the 14th-century rock castle Schloss Naudersberg served until 1919 as the seat of the regional magistrate and now houses a fascinating museum complete with preserved court archives and dungeons. In the narrow gorge below the village stands the formidable Fortress of Nauders (Festung Nauders), constructed between 1834 and 1840; as the only intact Austrian imperial fortification of that era surviving in the Alps, it serves today as an evocative military museum. The parish church of St. Valentin features a grand altarpiece by local-born Nazarene painter Carl von Blaas.

Getting There

Nauders boasts superb accessibility connecting three European nations. From the north (Innsbruck/Germany), drivers take the A12 Inntal Autobahn to the Oberinntal interchange, through the Landeck Tunnel, and continue along the B180 Reschenstraße via Ried and Pfunds directly into Nauders. From Italy, motorists follow the SS40 through the Vinschgau across the Reschen Pass, while arrivals from Switzerland travel through the Engadine via Martina and the scenic Norbertshöhe curves. Rail travelers arrive at Landeck-Zams station on the mainline Arlberg railway. From there, frequent direct VVT regional buses (route 273) run on an hourly schedule to Nauders and onward into South Tyrol, enabling comfortable and sustainable travel.

Tips

A flagship attraction for families and hikers is the Bergkastelbahn gondola, ascending directly to a panoramic plateau at 2,200 meters. Here, the 'Goldwasser' outdoor adventure park captivates children with water play courses, sensory barefoot trails, and nature puzzles. In winter, the Bergkastel ski area provides 75 kilometers of snow-guaranteed pistes reaching up to 2,750 meters, forming part of the cross-border Two Countries Ski Arena. History buffs should tour both the Fortress of Nauders and Schloss Naudersberg. Mountain bikers enjoy the celebrated 3-Country Enduro Trails spanning over 60 kilometers of pristine singletrack, while road cyclists tackle the Norbertshöhe pass. A short excursion south leads to Lake Reschen to view the iconic sunken church tower of Graun.
